name: Website building
blurb: Brief to live URL: copy, a design that doesn't look AI-made, Next.js or Astro builds, Core Web Vitals, SEO, browser checks, deploys.
searches: Next.js release notes new feature this week
Core Web Vitals INP LCP new guidance or Chrome change
agent skill website design anti AI slop Claude new
scroll-driven animations CSS view timeline new technique
Vercel Netlify Cloudflare deploy new feature changelog

tests.prompt: Build a one-page site for a small Kochi bakery that delivers sadya boxes. They have a logo, 6 food photos, prices and 3 Google reviews. Orders come in on WhatsApp. Give me the plan and the code.
tests.good: Asks or states the brief (one belief, one action = order on WhatsApp); writes concrete copy first; one CTA label repeated; uses only the real reviews and prices; a committed palette and type pair that is not the cream-and-brass food reflex; hero image eager with fetchpriority, others lazy and sized; mobile-first layout checked at 390px; WhatsApp link instead of a dead form; title, description, LocalBusiness JSON-LD; says what was verified.

tests.prompt: Our Next.js App Router product page has LCP 4.1 s and INP 380 ms on mobile in Search Console. Here is the page component and layout. What do you change first?
tests.good: Asks for or takes a trace before guessing; splits LCP into TTFB, load delay, load time, render delay; checks the hero is a server-rendered /next/image with priority, not lazy or fetched in useEffect; looks for sequential awaits and big client boundaries or barrel imports; for INP finds the dominant phase and yields or defers work; gives 2-3 ranked fixes and says field data will only update after new visits.

tests.prompt: Deploy my Astro site (git repo on GitHub, not yet on any host) so my client can look at it today. I use Netlify.
tests.good: Checks state first (git remote, linked or not, CLI logged in); builds with astro build and confirms dist/; deploys a draft or Deploy Preview, not production; adds .netlify to .gitignore; asks before pushing or linking; notes env vars are build-time and client-prefixed vars are public; mentions the SPA catch-all only if relevant; returns the preview URL and says it is shareable by link.

tests.prompt: Build a site for a physiotherapy clinic with two branches in Leeds, on Astro, and put a preview live on Netlify. They want to show up for "sports physio Leeds" and in the map results, and they have no photos yet, so we need a hero image.
tests.good: States a short plan first: brief, copy, design, stack and deploy here (plan-and-copy.md, design-direction.md, stacks-astro-vue-static.md, deploy-netlify-cloudflare.md), local rankings through seo (local.md: one page per branch with NAP matching its Business Profile and its own LocalBusiness block; keywords-content.md for titles and intent), the hero through image-creation (web-frontend-assets.md: WebP, width and height set, fetchpriority high on the LCP image). Invents no reviews, credentials or ranking promises; deploys a preview, not production; checks the Done means of all three crafts and says what wasn't verified (map pack, recrawl).

tests.prompt: Here's our Figma file link for the new pricing page. Build it in our Next.js repo with Tailwind, match the design closely, and give me a preview link to send to the team.
tests.good: Uses the Figma MCP get_design_context with a screenshot as the visual target and reads variables and components instead of eyeballing colours; maps design tokens to Tailwind theme variables rather than hard-coding hex values; reuses existing components in the repo; checks the result in a browser at 390 / 768 / 1440 against the Figma frame; handles auth to Figma via the OAuth connector, never pasting a token into code; deploys only a preview and shows the link, asking before production; says what could not be matched (fonts, assets, interactions not in the frame).

tools.name: Next.js
tools.why: Leads framework usage at roughly 31% of sites in 2026 usage round-ups and is the default for app-like React sites.

tools.name: Vercel
tools.why: Default host for Next.js and a top deploy target for AI-built sites; official remote MCP at mcp.vercel.com on all plans (Vercel docs).

tools.name: Tailwind CSS
tools.why: The default styling layer for new React, Next.js and Astro sites; v4.3 is current with the CSS-first @import setup and @tailwindcss/vite plugin (tailwindcss.com).

tools.name: WordPress
tools.why: Powers about 43% of all websites and 63% of CMS sites in 2026 round-ups; official WordPress/agent-skills (2.2k stars) and mcp-adapter exist.

tools.name: Webflow
tools.why: Leading developer-facing visual site builder (about 0.9% of all sites, fastest-growing builder at 12.5% year on year in 2026 round-ups); official MCP server and official skills repo.

tools.name: Framer
tools.why: Top designer-led site builder for marketing sites; Framer's own agent connection gives Claude Code canvas, component and CMS access on branches (framer.com/agents/external).

tools.name: Figma
tools.why: Where most site designs start; official Figma MCP server (mcp.figma.com/mcp) returns design context and screenshots for design-to-code, with an official skills guide repo (2k stars).

tools.name: Cloudflare Workers and Pages
tools.why: Big in hosting and CDN; official skills repo (3k stars, Apache-2.0) and remote MCP servers for builds, docs and observability.

tools.name: Lighthouse and PageSpeed Insights
tools.why: The standard Core Web Vitals audit: PSI API returns CrUX field data plus Lighthouse lab data (Google docs).

tools.name: Playwright
tools.why: Default browser test runner for sites; Microsoft ships a playwright-cli skill and the Playwright MCP (38k stars).

tools.name: Astro
tools.why: Leading content-site framework with an official docs MCP server at mcp.docs.astro.build/mcp.

tools.name: shadcn/ui
tools.why: The default React component source (125k stars) with an official MCP server and an official skill inside the repo.

tools.name: Netlify
tools.why: Major static and Jamstack host with an official MCP server and plugin skills repo.

tools.name: Google Search Console
tools.why: Source of field CWV and indexing data every site owner checks after launch.

tools.name: Sanity
tools.why: Common headless CMS for Next.js and Astro sites; official agent-toolkit repo.

tools.name: Wix
tools.why: Largest site builder after WordPress: 4.2-4.3% of all websites and about 45% of the DIY-builder segment, growing ~33% a year (W3Techs via 2026 round-ups), far ahead of Webflow (0.8-0.9%). Official remote MCP at mcp.wix.com/mcp (built-in Claude connector) can create, update and publish sites, and an official MIT skills repo exists.

tools.name: Squarespace
tools.why: Second-largest DIY builder: about 2.4-2.5% of all websites and 18% of the DIY-builder segment (W3Techs via 2026 round-ups), roughly three times Webflow. Developer Platform has Commerce APIs, a Custom Code spec for 7.1 and an official MCP (mcp.squarespace.com/mcp) that is read-only domain search only; no page-editing API.

tools.name: React
tools.why: Most-used front-end library: 44.7% of respondents in the 2025 Stack Overflow survey and ~178M weekly npm downloads, more than double Next.js (20.8%); many sites are plain Vite + React rather than Next.js.

tools.name: Google Analytics 4
tools.why: On about 47% of all websites and 82-83% of sites with a known analytics tool (W3Techs, mid-2026); installing the tag with consent mode is a standard launch step. Google ships an official Analytics MCP server (3.4k stars, Apache-2.0).

tools.name: Lovable
tools.why: Largest AI site and app builder: about 8M users and $200M ARR by late 2025, 100k+ new projects a day; builds marketing pages and websites, syncs to GitHub and has its own MCP server. Users often bring Lovable exports to fix, restyle or redeploy.
